gaps.sentence: He stayed ___ touch with every colleague he'd ever had.
The party is ___ the 14th, not the 21st.
___ the whole, the feedback was positive.
The proposal was rejected ___ a single vote.
gaps.explanation: 'by a single vote / by two goals' — the margin takes 'by'.

gaps.sentence: Given the budget, a new stadium is ___ of the question.
gaps.explanation: 'Out of the question' = not even worth considering.'

gaps.sentence: The negotiations broke down ___ the very brink of success.
gaps.explanation: 'on the brink of' = on the point of.

gaps.sentence: ___ terms of quality, the cheaper model wins.
The surgeons operated ___ the light of head-torches when the power failed.
gaps.explanation: 'By the light of' = using the light from something.
